description: Enable Run new terminals in the background in Settings → Terminal before opening a local terminal to keep it running after Muxy quits.
After enabling background sessions and opening a new local terminal, right-click inside its unpinned terminal-only tab and choose Send to Background to close the tab without stopping its processes.

Enable Free idle inactive terminals in Settings → Terminal to reclaim memory. Local terminals without a background session reopen a fresh shell in the same folder; background-session terminals reattach.
Enable Auto-copy selected text in Settings → Terminal to copy a terminal selection as soon as you release the mouse.
Command-click a file path in a local terminal, or a link in any terminal, to open it.
Right-click normally opens Muxy's terminal menu. If a program running inside the terminal has mouse reporting enabled and receives the click instead, use Shift-right-click.
By default, ⌘⌥↩ maximizes the selected split pane. Press it again to restore the full layout.
By default, ⌘⌥ plus an arrow key focuses a neighboring split pane.
By default, Control-Tab and Control-Shift-Tab focus the next or previous visible pane across the current layout.
Hold ⌘ and drag inside a terminal to move its pane to another area or create a split.
Right-click a tab to pin, recolor, rename, or close the tabs to its left, right, or all other tabs.
By default, ⌘I opens the Composer for multiline text, files, and images that you can send to the focused terminal.
Use Send Without Enter in the Composer's More menu to send text to the selected target—either the active pane or all split panes—without sending a Return keystroke.

With an on-device dictation language installed and microphone and speech recognition access allowed, ⌘⇧I starts dictation by default while the Composer is open. Stop dictation or press Return to insert the transcript at the cursor.
By default, in a browser tab, press ⌘⌥I or choose Inspect Element from the right-click menu to open Web Inspector.
Create browser profiles in Settings → Browser to keep cookies and logins separate, or import cookies from Chrome.
By default, ⌘⌥O searches open tabs, ⌘⌥P projects, ⌘⌥W worktrees, and ⌘⌥S workspaces.
Create reusable commands in Settings → Commands. By default, ⌘⇧P opens their picker.
Assign a global shortcut in Settings → Quick Terminal to open it from any app while Muxy runs. Double Shift requires Input Monitoring; its shell stays alive while hidden.
In a local workspace, open Add Project → Recently Removed to restore a removed project whose folder still exists, without changing its files.
Install the muxy CLI from the Muxy menu to script splits, send keys, and read visible terminal output. [Read the CLI docs](https://muxy.app/docs/features/muxy-cli).
Muxy can track supported coding agents and notify you when a turn finishes or needs input. Check Settings → Notifications.
Write an extension to replace the Muxy sidebar entirely. [Read the sidebar extension docs](https://muxy.app/docs/extensions/sidebars).
Extensions can add tabs, panels, popovers, top-bar and status-bar items, palette commands, and workspace automation. [Read the extension docs](https://muxy.app/docs/extensions/overview).
